q: Southampton were founded in 1885 by members of which organisation?
o: St Mary's Church of England Young Men's Association
hint: The church origin is why they are the Saints, and why the ground they moved to in 2001 is called St Mary's.

q: Southampton won the FA Cup in 1976 by beating which club in the final?
hint: Southampton were a Second Division side at the time, which made it one of the great final upsets.

q: Who scored the goal that won Southampton the 1976 FA Cup final?
hint: Stokes struck the only goal late on at Wembley; all four men played in that final.

q: Which manager led Southampton to that 1976 FA Cup triumph?
hint: McMenemy managed the club for 12 years and all four listed men held the job at some point.

q: Which ground did Southampton leave in 2001 after 103 years?
hint: The Dell was one of the smallest grounds in the Premier League before the move to St Mary's.

q: Matt Le Tissier spent his entire professional career at Southampton. What was he most renowned for?
hint: He converted 47 of the 48 penalties he took for the club — the one he missed was saved by Nottingham Forest's Mark Crossley.

q: Which future England captain scored a hat-trick on his full Southampton debut in 1988, aged 17?
hint: Shearer's treble came against Arsenal and made him the youngest player to score a top-flight hat-trick at that time.

q: Southampton lost the 2003 FA Cup final to which club?
hint: Robert Pires scored the only goal of the final in Cardiff.

q: Which manager left Southampton for Tottenham Hotspur in 2014?
hint: Pochettino spent a season and a half at St Mary's; Koeman succeeded him and later left for Everton.

q: Virgil van Dijk joined Southampton in 2015 from which club?
hint: He moved from Celtic to St Mary's, then to Liverpool in January 2018 for what was then a world-record fee for a defender.

q: Sadio Mané joined Southampton in 2014 from which club?
hint: He arrived from Salzburg and spent two seasons at St Mary's before joining Liverpool in 2016.

q: Southampton entered administration in 2009, suffering what immediate sporting punishment?
hint: The deduction was applied as they dropped into the third tier, deepening a fall that began with relegation from the Premier League in 2005.

q: Which of these England internationals came through Southampton's academy?
hint: Walcott left for Arsenal in 2006 aged 16; the academy also produced Gareth Bale, Adam Lallana and Luke Shaw.

q: Gareth Bale began his professional career at Southampton in which position?
hint: He broke through as a left-back and only became an attacking player after moving to Tottenham.

q: Southampton's fiercest rivalry, known as the South Coast derby, is with which club?
hint: The two cities are under 20 miles apart, and the fixture has often been played across different divisions.

q: Which England forward, later a racehorse trainer, is Southampton's record league goalscorer?
hint: Channon scored 185 league goals across two spells and became a successful trainer after retiring.

q: Which European Footballer of the Year joined Southampton in 1980, a signing that stunned English football?
hint: Keegan arrived from Hamburg as reigning Ballon d'Or holder and stayed two seasons.

q: What was Southampton's highest ever finish in the English top flight?
hint: They finished runners-up in 1983-84 under Lawrie McMenemy, three points behind Liverpool.

q: Which stadium has been Southampton's home since 2001?
hint: The name returns the club to its founding church, St Mary's, whose YMA formed the side in 1885.

q: James Ward-Prowse, Southampton's long-serving captain, became renowned for which skill?
hint: He studied David Beckham's technique and became one of the Premier League's most prolific free-kick scorers.
